canonical_fact: A JAM header commits to ancestry, prior state, extrinsic data, time, epoch/ticket/offender markers, block author and Bandersnatch signatures.

relations.statement: The header commits to the prior state through the prior-state Merkle root.
The header commits to extrinsic data through the extrinsic hash.

title: Block header

canonical_fact: Each non-genesis header cryptographically references its parent header by hash.
misconceptions: A JAM block can omit its parent reference if the state root is present.
title: Parent hash

canonical_fact: A JAM header contains the Merkle root of the prior state, which is also the parent block's posterior state; this supports pipelining of computation and Merklization.
misconceptions: The JAM header stores the posterior state root in the same way as Ethereum.
title: Prior state root

canonical_fact: The header's extrinsic hash is a Merkle commitment to the block's extrinsic data, with structure supporting inclusion proofs for reports and preimages.
title: Extrinsic hash

canonical_fact: Each block header carries a timeslot index; a valid block's slot must be strictly later than its parent's and not in the future.
misconceptions: A block with a future JAM timeslot is permanently invalid and can never become valid later.

relations.statement: Safrole assigns block-authoring rights per six-second timeslot.

title: Timeslot

canonical_fact: JAM measures protocol time from 12:00 UTC on January 1, 2025, with slots indexed from that common era.
title: JAM Common Era

canonical_fact: Safrole operates on six-second timeslots for block production.
title: Slot duration

canonical_fact: Safrole groups timeslots into epochs and rotates validator/ticket-related state at epoch boundaries.

relations.statement: Each epoch has a slot-sealer sequence covering its possible block slots.

title: Epoch

canonical_fact: The optional epoch marker carries key and entropy information relevant to the following epoch, including fallback operation.
title: Epoch marker

canonical_fact: The optional winning-tickets marker supplies the slot-sealing tickets for the next epoch when the ticket contest succeeds.
title: Winning-tickets marker

canonical_fact: The header offenders marker lists newly misbehaving validators by Ed25519 key.

relations.statement: Offender information can cause later validator-set entries to be replaced by the null key.

title: Offenders marker

canonical_fact: The block author is identified by an index into the posterior active validator set.
misconceptions: The block header stores the author’s complete validator key tuple directly instead of an index.
title: Block author index

canonical_fact: The header seal is a Bandersnatch signature proving the designated slot sealer authorized the block.
title: Block seal

canonical_fact: The header includes a Bandersnatch VRF-style signature whose output contributes bias-resistant protocol entropy.
title: Entropy VRF signature

canonical_fact: JAM state is explicitly partitioned into largely independent components so that parts of the block transition can be computed in parallel where dependencies permit.
title: State partitioning
